Thanks for the initial RFI packet. We reviewed the deployment summary and have a couple of follow-up clarifying questions before we proceed to the evidence packet phase:

1) Reachability scope: can you confirm which control-plane endpoints (by role) are reachable from customer VPCs versus strictly internal operator networks? We're particularly interested in any sidecar/proxy endpoints that accept inbound connections from tenant subnets.

2) Operator choreography: RidgeBank requires a short narrative that explains how operator actions (scaling, software updates, emergency maintenance) are performed without introducing new cross-tenant reachability—i.e., what temporary tunnels/bastions, if any, are used and how they are audited.

Could you provide a network diagram that highlights the reachability boundaries, a short summary of the operator choreography, and a CSV/xlsx reachability matrix (component x origin) by EOD Friday if possible?

We'll share this with our SOC and procurement for the next stage. If a short call would help, I'm available Thursday afternoon PST.

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear questions. Attached are three artifacts that should address your asks: ridgebank-network-diagram-v2.png (annotated), reachability-matrix.xlsx, and a short operator-choreography-excerpt.pdf (2 pages). Summary answers below: 

1) Reachability scope (short):
- Customer VPCs can initiate TLS connections only to the public ingress layer (tenant-proxy endpoints) and to allowlisted egress endpoints (for outbound logging/metrics).
- Control-plane operator endpoints (orchestration API, deployment control channels) sit in a separate control VLAN and are not directly reachable from tenant subnets.
- Sidecars (inference-sidecar) accept inbound requests only from the local host network or from the tenant-proxy via mTLS; they do not listen on public-facing interfaces.

2) Operator choreography (short):
- Routine operations use an operator console in the control-plane VPC; changes are executed through a mediation API that requires operator identity (Okta SSO + MFA) and are logged to an immutable audit stream.
- For maintenance requiring remote access, operators create ephemeral session tokens via a jump-proxy service; the session is timeboxed, recorded, and automatically revoked when the maintenance window closes.
- No operator-initiated inbound tunnels are left open to tenant networks—maintenance traffic is pulled into isolated maintenance partitions or proxied via short-lived, mutually authenticated channels.

Next steps: happy to run a 30-min walkthrough and share the annotated diagram live. Our Drive link is: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1r-example-redwood-ridgebank-rfi.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez

Alex — attaching the finalized artifacts and an executive summary for your packet. Highlights: 

- Reachability: tenant subnets can only reach tenant-proxy endpoints over mTLS; control-plane management endpoints are partitioned into a control VLAN with no inbound routes from tenant address spaces. See attached ridgebank-network-diagram-v2.png and reachability-matrix.xlsx for component-by-origin details.

- Operator choreography: all operator actions are mediated via authenticated APIs; ephemeral maintenance sessions are brokered through a recorded jump-proxy and are time-limited. A short excerpt describing the audit trail and evidence pointers is attached (operator-choreography-excerpt.pdf).

- KV cache & data isolation: per-tenant cache namespaces, access controls, and encryption-at-rest are documented in the excerpt. We also included a short note on our fallback policy (model variant fallback) clarifying that fallbacks use pre-authorized internal channels and do not open new inbound connections into tenant networks.

Attachments: ridgebank-network-diagram-v2.png (annotated), reachability-matrix.xlsx, operator-choreography-excerpt.pdf
